Subject: POC runway: performance guardrail and extension request

Hi David,

Thanks again for the support during our ingestion pilot — the model throughput has been great and the devs appreciate the latency tuning notes from Marcus. We hit our internal milestone but need a slightly longer evaluation window to validate production traffic shape (roughly +3 weeks). Before we lock an extension I wanted to discuss two things:

1) A short-term SLA guardrail if we move to a longer timebox (we're sensitive to tail latency spikes during large batch ingests).
2) How a small conversion incentive or introductory discount might look if we commit to a production pilot within 60 days of the extended evaluation.

Can you share a pragmatic structure (pricing + credits) that protects us if performance regresses during the extended pilot but still gives Redwood visibility to convert? We don’t want a heavy legal redline — something operational and measurable is best.

Attached is our last 72h ingest sample and a short note on expected traffic.

Thanks,
Eleni
CTO, Archival.ai

Hi Eleni — really glad the team saw the performance uplift. Happy to structure something pragmatic. High level proposal below; if this aligns I’ll loop in Kimberly for pricing/legal signoff and send a short amendment.

Proposal (extension = +21 days):
- Price: keep current timeboxed POC rate for the extension (no extra charge for the 3-week window).
- Conditional performance guardrail (operational SLA credit):
  - Metric: 95th percentile latency for the ingest + generation pipeline measured on your test traffic curve.
  - Trigger: if 95p exceeds 600ms for 3 consecutive measurement windows (weekly aggregates) during the extension, Redwood issues a credit equal to 15% of the extension's billed amount (one-time credit applied to next invoice).
- Conversion incentive: if Archival.ai signs a production Dedicated or Hosted commitment within 60 days of the extension end date, Redwood will apply a one-time conversion credit equal to 25% of the first month’s committed spend (credit applied after first invoice).
- Operational notes: Redwood will provide weekly summary reports (CSV) and a short RCA for any trigger event. Credits are purely commercial (no SLA termination or service credits beyond the stated percentage).

If you want tighter guardrails we can increase the measurement cadence or change the threshold; I kept it intentionally simple to avoid lengthy redlines. I’ve attached a draft proposal that captures the numbers — Marcus, any technical caveats you want called out before I send to Kimberly?

Thanks,
David
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposal_Archival_v2.pdf (pdf, 142 KB)]
